title: Stress-test an argument politely
goal: Use counterarguments to find assumptions, not to outsource your judgement.
explanation: An AI opponent can generate plausible objections but may invent evidence. Define the claim narrowly, separate empirical statements from values and ask what evidence would change each side’s view. A useful debate ends with a revised claim or a better question, not a manufactured winner.
sampleInput: Claim: “Remote work is always better than office work.” Context: a fictional eight-person design team; two members need physical workshop equipment, three prefer quiet home working, and the team has missed two handovers. No productivity study is supplied.
prompt: Challenge the word “always” in this claim using only the supplied context. Give one strongest counterexample, one assumption to test and one fair question. Do not fabricate studies or diagnose people. After I answer, help me rewrite a narrower, testable claim.
workedExample: Counterexample: equipment-dependent tasks may require a shared workshop. Revised claim: for suitable desk tasks, a hybrid arrangement might help this team if handover reliability is maintained. That is a proposal to test, not a proven productivity result.

steps.title: State the claim
steps.text: Mark absolute words and define which team and tasks you mean.

steps.title: Request a steelman objection
steps.text: Ask for the strongest reasonable counterexample rather than insults or rhetorical tricks.

steps.title: Audit evidence
steps.text: Label each statement source-supported, hypothetical or unsupported; remove fabricated study references.

steps.title: Answer one question
steps.text: Explain which trade-off matters most and what measurement you would accept.

steps.title: Revise and plan a test
steps.text: Write a narrower claim and two measures, such as handover completion and task cycle time.

checks: The objection targets an identifiable assumption rather than the speaker.
No invented study or unsupported productivity number is accepted as evidence.
The final claim has a scope and a plausible way to test it.
commonMistakes: Equating persuasive language with a true counterargument.
Treating the exercise as a competition to “destroy” an opponent.
offline: Write the strongest objection yourself, then ask a partner to improve it respectfully.
reflection: What evidence could genuinely make you change your mind?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. The objection targets an identifiable assumption rather than the speaker.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. No invented study or unsupported productivity number is accepted as evidence.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Equating persuasive language with a true counterargument.
